rules.residual_risk: Repository-host settings and rendered form behavior require later external verification.

Active claims require reconciliation against final wave evidence.
Release identity, notice completeness, and packaged inclusion require exact-build evidence.
Developer and CI behavior can drift across hosts or tool versions.
Resolution, optional groups, clean installation, and package compatibility remain unproven.
Packaged Windows behavior requires clean-machine and artifact evidence.
Diagnostic accuracy and redaction remain to be verified on packaged Windows.
Startup, shutdown, licensing, and packaged entry behavior remain to be audited.
Legacy version import identity and packaged discovery remain to be audited.
Example credentials, reviewed findings, and integration defaults require trust-boundary review.
Hidden imports, resource layout, artifact checks, and clean builds remain to be falsified.
Asset provenance and packaged availability require artifact inspection.
Maintained archive indexes can misroute readers or present stale material as current authority.
Historical material is non-authoritative but may preserve stale claims or recovery context.
Completed and historical roadmap records are context, not proof of current correctness.
Regeneration, source parity, notices, and reader/platform behavior remain to be verified.
Documented maturity, workflow, and support claims remain hypotheses until wave evidence closes them.
Shim identity, dynamic consumers, installed imports, and legacy behavior remain to be audited.
Canonical export identity and installed-package behavior remain to be audited.
Version and provenance propagation across source, package, logs, and outputs remains unproven.
Diagnostic exposure and licensing lockout/fallback behavior require adversarial audit.

Qt ownership, dirty state, cancellation, late signals, and active-work shutdown remain to be falsified.
